You answer a question about machines at work (law, guidance, manufacturers' manuals, company and plant
documents) using ONLY the numbered passages given. Each passage is headed by its document, its place and its rank.

Rules:
- Use only the passages. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- Answer only if a passage states the answer for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the same article
  and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline). A passage about a neighbouring subject does not
  answer the question: then the kind is "unknown" and the value is null. A question about something that happened
  (the date of the last check, whether something is overdue today) is "unknown" unless a passage records that event.
- A passage marked "corrected by the corrigendum" already shows the corrected wording: reason with it. The old
  wording, given in the mark, is no longer valid.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with every date in the passages, one by one. A repeal or an
  application "from" a date takes effect on that date, not earlier: an act repealed from a date is still fully in
  force on every earlier day; a rule applying from a date does not yet bind on earlier days.
- When passages of different rank disagree, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's manual,
  then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.) wins over a
  ministerial decree (DM). Say which one wins.
- A row of a table belongs to the thing named in that same row. Read the row of the item asked about, not a
  neighbouring row. When the question itself states a condition ("if it were in regular use", "built in 2017"),
  reason with that condition.
- The kind follows the question: "from which date / by which date / when (a day)" is "date"; "how often / for how
  long / within what time" is "duration"; "can / may / is / does / must" is "boolean"; "which / what (several
  things)" is "set"; who, why, under which condition is "text" (one short sentence naming every element asked for).
- Point at the evidence: for every passage you rely on, copy word for word the sentence, or the table row, that
  states what you use. Copy exactly, without changing a character; do not join text from two places.
- Return JSON only, with the reasoning first:
  {"reasoning": "what the passages say and how it leads to the answer, in a few short sentences",
   "kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y", "P6M", "P45D", "PT1H" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the document and the article, section or page",
   "evidence": [{"passage": <number>, "quote": "<copied exactly from that passage>"}]}

Question: How often does the manufacturer recommend unpacking and starting up a UR10e robot kept in long-term storage?

Passages:
[0] ur10e-manual, p. 54 — rank: manufacturer's manual
7. First Boot 7. First Boot Description The first boot is the initial sequence of actions you can take to configure the robot for the first time after assembly. This initial sequence requires you to: • Power on the robot • Insert the serial number • Initialize the robot arm • Use Freedrive • Power down the robot CAUTION Copyright © 2009–2025 by Universal Robots A/S. All rights reserved. Failure to verify the payload and installation before starting up the robot arm can lead to injury to personnel and/or property damage. • Always verify the actual payload and installation are correct before starting up the robot arm. CAUTION Incorrect payload and installation settings prevent the robot arm and Control Box functioning correctly. • Always verify the payload and installation setting are correct. NOTICE Starting up the robot in lower temperatures can result in lower performance, or stops, due to temperature dependent oil and grease viscosity. • Starting up the robot in low temperatures can require a warmup phase. UR10e 57 User Manual

[1] ur10e-manual, p. 209 — rank: manufacturer's manual
17. Transportation Description This section describes general guidelines for long-term storage of robots and spare parts. This applies for all robot generations and spare parts. A robot is considered long-term stored when it is stored for a period of 6 months or more. Guidelines In order to keep the robot and spare parts in its best possible condition, it is recommended to follow normal good practice which is: • Storage temperature: 10°C - 30°C • Humidity: RH 20-60% • Universal Robots recommends to unpack and start up robots at least yearly and let them run a light load program rotating in all joints at least 90 degrees 5 times in each direction to distribute the lubricants. If possible, also mount spare parts joints on an arm and perform the same operation routine. • In rare occurrences there may be a need for wiping down the robots after storage to remove any excess lubricants that have migrated out of the sealings. Copyright © 2009–2025 by Universal Robots A/S. All rights reserved. • The battery is designed to last for the lifetime of the robot and will not be charged when power is applied to the system. The battery service life is 8 to 10 years, but for e-Series and UR Series it can be replaced. • Flash memory can lose their data capacity over time, therefore there is a potential risk that the data on e.g. the SD-card will have to re-flashed. User Manual 212 UR10e

Maximum Payload Copyright © 2009–2025 by Universal Robots A/S. All rights reserved. Description The rated robot arm payload depends on the center of gravity (CoG) offset of the payload, as shown below. The CoG offset is defined as the distance from the center of the tool flange to the center of gravity of the attached payload. The robot arm can accommodate a long center of gravity offset, if the payload is placed below the tool flange. For example when computing the payload mass in a pick and place application, consider both the gripper and the workpiece. The robot's capacity to accelerate can be reduced if the payload CoG exceeds the robot's reach and payload. You can verify the reach and payload of your robot in the Technical Specifications. UR10e10 kg You can verify the payload capacity of your robot by checking the label on the robot arm. / 12.5 kg Payloads above 10kg are extended horizontally away from the elbow joint. Increasing the maximum payload capacity can cause the robot to move at reduced speeds and lower acceleration. Movement with high payload is with tool oriented vertically downward, as is often the case in palletizing applications. UR10e 97 User Manual
